basis: Gluconeogenesis disorder; liver dysfunction and neurodevelopmental impairment occur in 5-29%. Frequent transaminase elevations alone do not establish lasting hepatic damage.

decisions.hepatic: none: liver dysfunction and steatosis occur in 5-29%; ALT/AST elevation at 30-79% alone does not establish lasting hepatic injury.

basis: Neurodevelopmental impairment defines disease; Pierre-Robin sequence with mandibular malformation is reported in 9/9. Pigmentation and minor facial features do not establish additional damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: Pierre-Robin sequence establishes mandibular malformation, but cleft palate or independent gastrointestinal tissue damage is not documented.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: Pierre-Robin sequence in 9/9 includes mandibular hypoplasia, a consequential congenital skeletal malformation.

basis: Cestode infection; intestinal adult-tapeworm infections constitute most cases across the umbrella. Tissue-invasive larval forms affect variable organs.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: intestinal infections account for most patients across cestodiases; extraintestinal larval infections do not establish another shared organ.

basis: Leukocyte adhesion dysfunction; lymphocytic interstitial pneumonia and inflammatory stomatitis/gingivitis each occur in 30-79%. Separately diagnosed infections are excluded.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: recurrent aphthous stomatitis and gingivitis occur in 30-79%, supporting direct inflammatory oral injury; oral thrush alone would not qualify.

basis: Stalk-containing spinal meningocele defines neural/meningeal dysraphism; the spina bifida cystica ancestry establishes a vertebral closure defect.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: the vertebral arch closure defect of spina bifida cystica is part of this congenital spinal malformation.

basis: Astrocytic neurodegeneration defines disease. Scoliosis, despite HPO frequency of 80-99%, is secondary to motor dysfunction; eye-movement and swallowing abnormalities are neurologic.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: scoliosis is a secondary, separately diagnosed deformity rather than direct skeletal injury by the astrocytic disease, despite its 80-99% annotation.

basis: Partial 20q duplication commonly causes developmental delay/intellectual disability. Skeletal malformations vary with the duplicated interval; a shared damaging skeletal phenotype is unestablished.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: skeletal abnormalities vary across duplication intervals; neither a defining skeletal lesion nor damaging involvement in at least 30% is established.

basis: Eyelid, eye-movement and lacrimal defects define syndrome; tricuspid regurgitation occurs in 30-79%. Common minor skeletal dysmorphism does not establish functional skeletal damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: maxillary hypoplasia and clinodactyly occur in 80-99%, but are described as minor dysmorphism without established skeletal functional impairment.

basis: Pancreatic beta-cell insulin excess defines disease; persistent neurodevelopmental impairment from neuroglycopenic injury affects roughly 30-50% in severe resistant congenital hyperinsulinism.

decisions.neurologic: involved: lasting neuroglycopenic injury or developmental impairment affects approximately 30-50% in severe resistant disease; this is direct metabolic injury.

basis: Lymphatic malformation, intestinal lymphangiectasia and ID define syndrome. Immune depletion occurs in 80-99%; cap excludes lymphopenia (80-99%) and glaucoma (30-79%).

decisions.neurologic: primary: intellectual disability is explicitly part of the syndrome's definition and occurs in 80-99%.
decisions.infectious_immune: involved: immunoglobulin depletion occurs in 80-99% from lymphatic/enteric losses; secondary immune dysfunction is an organ consequence of the lymphatic disorder.
